name: FlowSOM tree
description: Draws FlowSOM's tree (minimum spanning tree) with star, number, pie and per-marker views, and the stars on the SOM grid, from the model a FlowSOM step (flowsom_operator >= 2.2.0) writes. The tree is FlowSOM's own: built from the map's codes, not re-estimated from the cell labels.

properties.name: node_factor
properties.description: Column factor holding each cell's SOM node (cluster_id of the FlowSOM step). Empty: the one column factor whose name ends in cluster_id.

properties.name: population_factor
properties.description: Column factor naming each cell's population. Each node is coloured by the population most of its cells have. Empty: colour by metacluster.

properties.name: group_factor
properties.description: Column factor for the pies: each node's cells split by this factor (for example disease group). Empty: no pie plot.

properties.name: plots
properties.description: Which plots, comma-separated: stars (stars on the tree), numbers (node numbers on the tree), grid (stars on the SOM grid), pies (cells per group on the tree), markers (one tree per marker).

properties.name: markers
properties.description: Markers for the per-marker trees, comma-separated. Empty: every marker of the model.

properties.name: marker_label_factor
properties.description: Row factor to name the markers by (for example c.antigen), when the FlowSOM step's first row factor is the FCS channel. Empty: the names in the model.

properties.name: population_palette
properties.description: Palette for populations, assigned to the sorted population names, as Tercen's Plot operator does: tab20, tab10, Palette-1, Set1 or Dark2.

properties.name: group_palette
properties.description: Palette for the pie groups (sorted): tab20, tab10, Palette-1, Set1 or Dark2.

metaFactors.name: Model
metaFactors.description: The channel and the flowsom_model column of a FlowSOM (>= 2.2.0) step. The model is the same on every row.

metaFactors.name: Cells
metaFactors.description: The cells, with the FlowSOM node (cluster_id) and optionally a population and a group factor.
